description: One entry on the dock -- what it points at, its order (`idx`) and whether it is hidden. The same rows at all three layers: an app's fragment, the site's arrangement and one person's own are told apart by the parent `Dock`, never by the row. What an entry points at *is* its identity, and it is a typed Dynamic Link: a `type` saying which kind of thing and a name saying which one. Two columns where whichever was filled was the kind is what this replaces -- a third kind of entry now costs a row value rather than a column.

fields.description: Which kind of thing this entry opens: a `Sidebar` or a `Workspace`. An open Link to `DocType` rather than a Select, because the schema is not what closes the set -- `Dock` whitelists the two explicitly, and a row naming any other doctype is refused rather than stored.
fields.label: Type

fields.description: The record this entry opens, in the doctype `type` names. A `Sidebar` row names a **module**: a sidebar is named by its title (`autoname: field:title`) and the title defaults to the module's name, so the module's own sidebar is what such a row lands on -- and a module whose sidebar is a computed base is nameable here too, because a dock row *names* what it opens rather than referencing it, which is why link validation on a `Dock` is a deliberate no-op. Spelled `link_name` and not `name` because a row's `name` is its own primary key: a docfield called that would be overwritten by autoname the moment the row was inserted.
fields.label: Name

fields.description: Kept in the row so an explicitly hidden entry stays hidden when its app later adds entries, instead of reappearing because it is simply absent.
fields.label: Hidden

name: Dock Item
